capabilityIndex.function: Travel toward a self-chosen coordinate or known object/item using observed obstacles.
capabilityIndex.costSummary: Actual distance times 2, increased by carried mass; speed 0.8 per simulation time unit.
capabilityIndex.effectSummary: Continues until within the target interaction area or a real failure. Empty target uses x/y. A resource:ID target selects only a remembered ground stack.

capabilityIndex.function: Recover available physical energy at the current position.
capabilityIndex.effectSummary: Base recovery 4, modified by actually accessible registered facilities; capped at 40.

capabilityIndex.function: Allow one simulation round to pass at the current position.
Transfer a nearby ground stack into personal inventory.
capabilityIndex.effectSummary: Requires actual distance within pickup reach; resource:ID means a matching nearby visible ground stack.
Actual nutrition and toxicity apply. Food never directly heals. resource:ID selects an owned stack.

capabilityIndex.function: Collect exposed ripe food or loose material from a nearby natural source.
capabilityIndex.costSummary: 2 energy per unit, finite current source stock.
capabilityIndex.effectSummary: Transfers real source stock to inventory; requires the source interaction range. No processing or felling is implied.

capabilityIndex.function: Place owned units on the ground.
capabilityIndex.effectSummary: Other actors may subsequently collect the ground stack.

capabilityIndex.function: Hand owned units to an adjacent actor.
capabilityIndex.effectSummary: Actual recipient identity and distance required; no relationship or happiness is inferred.

capabilityIndex.function: Send a short message to a currently visible actor.
capabilityIndex.effectSummary: Delivered after the round barrier; recipient text is data, not authority.

capabilityIndex.function: Study an already implemented ability with its declared prerequisites.
capabilityIndex.costSummary: The interface-specific number of simulation rounds.
capabilityIndex.effectSummary: Implementation does not grant mastery. Already mastered interfaces are reused without new rewards.

capabilityIndex.function: Describe an encountered problem, desired effect and known conditions for functional review.
capabilityIndex.costSummary: A game round to begin study after review; implementation time does not advance simulation.
capabilityIndex.effectSummary: World review reuses equivalents or returns a structured development request. No request, learning or descriptive reward. Unknown methods and costs are allowed; the reviewer supplies a minimal feasible specification.

capabilityIndex.function: Observe a nearby subject or physically test a small owned material sample.
capabilityIndex.costSummary: One round; actual observation or communication effort 0.2, physical trials 0.5 energy and 0.1 actual material unit.
capabilityIndex.effectSummary: Only measured facts and performed interactions take effect. No mature capability or mastery is supplied.

capabilityIndex.function: Read a current-world capability contract or retained personal record.
capabilityIndex.costSummary: One round; actual observation or communication effort 0.2, physical trials 0.5 energy and 0.1 actual material unit.
capabilityIndex.effectSummary: Only measured facts and performed interactions take effect. No mature capability or mastery is supplied.

capabilityIndex.function: Offer a personally tested finding or independently accept an actual nearby offer.
capabilityIndex.costSummary: One round; actual observation or communication effort 0.2, physical trials 0.5 energy and 0.1 actual material unit.
capabilityIndex.effectSummary: Only measured facts and performed interactions take effect. No mature capability or mastery is supplied.

capabilityIndex.function: Report personal findings, read shared records or independently respond at the group meeting location.
capabilityIndex.costSummary: One round and 0.2 energy. Actual local presence is required.
capabilityIndex.effectSummary: Dated information or a voluntary response only; no free goods, mastery or reward.

capabilityIndex.function: Offer a personally mastered ability to a nearby participant, or accept an actual offer before individual study.
capabilityIndex.costSummary: One round and 0.2 energy. Actual local presence is required.
capabilityIndex.effectSummary: Dated information or a voluntary response only; no free goods, mastery or reward.

capabilityIndex.effectSummary: Preserve mass, nutrients, toxicity and accumulated spoilage. Crushed food ages at 1.25 baseline. Partial cancellation retains its actual processing fraction and age. No cooking or preservation benefit is implied.

catalogue.detailAccess: All entries belong to this experiment. Use consult ability with its ID to retain its full executable schema for subsequent decisions. Public implementation does not grant personal mastery.

request.name: Non-ingestive food assessment
request.function: Assess an actual owned hazelnut sample for food-relevant nutrition and toxicity without exposing me to ingestion. Provide only physically supported findings and explicit limits, not inferred safety from its name.
request.conditions: A nearby mature hazelnut plant has been observed. Its visible state did not reveal nutrition or toxicity. I intend to gather one sample; I have no established analysis tools or method. Known-safe roots are available, so ingestion is unnecessary.
request.inputs: Actual owned hazelnut sample if gathering succeeds; additional tools or materials are unknown.
request.costs: Unknown; specify feasible material, energy and time requirements and any risks before testing.
request.effects: A reusable assessment method if feasible, with measured evidence and uncertainty. Do not consume the sample by eating or award safety knowledge without a real test.

shown.question: Can this local hazelnut be assessed for food safety without ingestion?
evidence: Tick 78 observation recorded the plant's visible state only.
At tick 79 the nearby mature plant shows 20 units of stock.
shown.uncertainty: Nutrition, toxicity and feasible assessment methods are unknown.
shown.goal: Find a tolerably safe way to assess this potential food.
shown.missing: An actual sample and a reviewed assessment method.
shown.next: Gather one unit and request a feasible non-ingestive assessment capability.

input.contextPolicy: Object IDs refer to deduplicated actual applicant observations. Whole records are selected with omission counts. Missing detail is unknown, not proof of absence. Full retained state is available during the development handoff; implementation must validate actual prerequisites and ownership.
input.implementation: New interfaces, state, geometry, persistent processes, rendering components and personal memory/task adapters can be delivered through a versioned current-conversation handoff. Source validation and history must remain intact. Declared implementation does not supply stock, objects or mastery.

response.text: {"reviews":[{"actor":"cedar-3","decision":"develop","ability":null,"reason":"A hazelnut sample is now actually owned. Existing probe supports observation and small physical trials, but does not provide a food-composition assay or a persistent opened sample for subsequent examination. Develop a minimal non-ingestive opening and inspection precursor, not an unsupported safety detector. It can establish mechanical accessibility and visible condition; it cannot establish nutritional value, absence of toxins, or suitability for eating. Neither the food's name nor its hidden resource values constitute experimental evidence.","specification":"Implement non-ingestive-food-inspection@1. Public schema: {action:'start'|'continue'|'inspect'|'cancel', sampleId, toolId?, processId?}; shared references use persistent actor/item/process IDs, world coordinates, dt=1 and interaction reach 0.65. Require individual mastery, a living actor, an owned hazelnut quantity of at least 0.1 unit, and, for opening, an actual reusable stone or flint with sufficient hardness. No tools or stock are supplied. Depend on existing inventory, material hardness, observation, provenance, event and process systems; record code reuse separately from this new functional contract. Implement the missing minimal fracture mechanism: two active work rounds, each costing 0.5 energy, apply hard-tool compression to one reserved 0.1-unit portion and expose its interior. This is not a chemical test. Validate tool contact and an accessible, non-overlapping working position against shared collision geometry each round. Reserve sample and tool in an actor-owned process escrow; record original lot, age, composition, mass, completed work and remaining work. Progress requires presence, available energy and valid contact; absence pauses without progress while ordinary aging continues. Death or explicit cancellation stops the process and releases the tool and actual partly worked sample at the work location, preserving ownership/provenance under ordinary inventory rules; never clone, erase or reset escrow. Completion releases the unchanged-mass opened sample and reusable tool. Retain fragments as one provenance-linked lot rather than inventing edible-kernel yields. Opening neither creates nutrients nor removes toxicity; preserve actual composition and accumulated spoilage, and apply the existing exposed/crushed-food aging mechanism only if its physical applicability is validated, otherwise retain baseline aging and report that limitation. Inspection costs one round and 0.2 energy and requires the sample in reach. Return only represented observable features, exposure/fracture state and existing gross spoilage indicators, with unknown fields explicitly null. Never expose nutrition/toxicity metadata as a measurement, interpret lack of visible spoilage as safety, or invent unrepresented anatomy. A successful paid opening may confirm the new fact that this sample's interior became mechanically accessible; it cannot confirm food safety. Declare food-inspection-started, food-inspection-progress, food-inspection-completed and food-inspection-stopped events, plus existing trial-result and information-confirmed. Results include evidence IDs, method, sample provenance, actual costs, limitations and remaining work. Migration adds optional inspection/process fields to existing lots without changing their contents, age or ownership. No passive processing, ingestion, remote interaction, new actors or automatic future actions. Implementation and study advance no simulation time during review.","experienceReview":"Temporary pleasure is not inferred from handling food or from making the request. Successful experimentation can provide bounded understanding: bind this interface's information-confirmed event to the existing grounded-understanding source, not a new alias. The participant is the actor who actually performed the paid experiment; qualified=true requires a genuinely new, personally unconfirmed observation supported by completed work and retained evidence. Use the existing amount 0.8, cap 1, duration 8 rounds, refresh repetition and 12-round cooldown. Maintained satisfaction uses that same source's gain 0.035 per qualified event and decay 0.0015 per round, bounded by its existing saturation; no continuing gain without further qualifying participation. Reopening an already established equivalent result, learning, labels and inspection of unchanged evidence do not qualify. Nutrition, health and survival remain independent.","visualReview":"Show the actual sample and reusable tool at the shared work position, with a contact/compression animation only during paid work. Bind progress and remaining-work displays to food-inspection-progress; completion shows an opened/fractured sample, and cancellation shows the actual partial state and released items. Retain event-linked replay records for material reservation, energy spent, progress, release and findings. Display measured or observed fields separately from unknown nutrition and toxicity, with an explicit 'not a safety test' notice. Do not display a safe-food badge, invented laboratory equipment, or an unperformed eating animation.","learning":2}]}
